newsitem.title: USA: Dole blasts Clinton on Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Dole blasts Clinton on Northern Ireland.

text.p: Republican Presidential candidate Bob Dole blasted President Bill Clinton's involvement in Northern Ireland peace efforts on Thursday as part of a full scale assualt on the president's foreign policy.
In a speech to businessmen he complained that even though the president "invited a terrorist to the White House" it did not lead to peace in Ireland.

The comment, an apparent reference to Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams whose White House visit sparked a major controversy, appeared to be an ad lib by Dole from prepared remarks. Sinn Fein is the political wing of the Irish Republican Army.
Dole listed a number of world trouble spots where he said Clinton claimed success but had really failed.

He said, "The Clinton administration has also claimed success in Northern Ireland. These claims of great strides toward peace appear unwarranted in the face of increased violence and terrorism in Northern Ireland and England."
The Clinton administration said that by granting a visa to Adams and talking to him it helped encourage the now broken IRA ceasefire.
